answer: Each identity registers one apiary: a numbered hive colony in a registered orchard, inspected yearly by the beekeepers' association. One colony backs one identity; a shared apiary or duplicate number merges both into one weight. Each fake costs one real colony: 480 units to buy and site, a 60-unit opal seal fee and 120 days of tending to pass; 100 fakes cost 54,000 units. The fable that one colony splits into many overnight fails: a fresh split has no brood pattern or yield history, copied logs fail the scale records, and one proven fake apiary revokes the cluster and bars the keeper.
